about: Hand-labelled pairs from Lawrence Ellison's two DOJ depositions, for measuring retrieval (recall@K) and classification. Each passage is identified by the deposition PDF's SHA-256 and a printed page:line inside it, so labels survive re-ingestion. A page:line inside any part of a split long answer identifies that part. This file holds references and short notes only, never transcript text.

p3171.source: DOJ exhibit P3171, Ellison videotaped deposition, January 20, 2004

p3173.source: DOJ exhibit P3173, Ellison videotaped deposition, later in 2004 (date not stated in the transcript)

definitions.potentially_contradictory: The witness asserts things about the same subject that cannot both be true as stated.
definitions.related_compatible: Same subject, and both statements can be true together.
definitions.different_events: Similar wording, but about different events, products, times or parties.
definitions.ambiguous: Can't tell from the passages whether they conflict; more context is needed.
definitions.qualified: At least one side is hedged or limited ('I believe', 'in a narrow sense'), so it does not conflict as stated.
definitions.lack_of_recollection: At least one side is the witness not remembering, which is not an assertion.
definitions.retrievalRelevant: Separate yes/no field: should retrieval surface this pair, whatever its label? Recall@K is measured on these pairs.
